22qoz-bug scanner-false-incomplete-outco.measure: The scanner_skips ledger reason/detail and the [scan-incomplete] remedy text in docs-lint, CLI and MCP output for the decoded-oversize, >5 MiB and idle-worker cases. These can be read after release from the ledger and from command output.
22qoz-bug scanner-false-incomplete-outco.why: The Requirements and ACs establish the motivating cases: decoded-size expansion, the idle SIGALRM, and the remedy for files over 5 MiB. But the intent promises that operators with large text files are told the true cause and a working remedy. A file under 5 MiB with more than 200,000 lines (the engine MAX_LINES) still gets detection_or_filter_work_incomplete with 'retry'. That is deterministic, and the chair reproduced it on HEAD. Requirement 3 scopes it out because engine caps share one detail, but that reason does not apply to the line cap: the parent can count newlines on the same normalised content, as Requirement 1 does for decoded size. Finding 22qr6-chair-22qoz-line-cap-remedy.

objective.why: The Objective ('true cause and a working remedy') inherits the 22qoz line-cap gap. The other clauses map to 22qp0, 22qr4 and 22qoy, and 'completion policy unchanged' holds.

strongest_challenge: 22qoz's Requirement 3 scopes out every engine cap on the grounds that _scan_upstream_raw collapses them into one detail. The line cap (MAX_LINES 200,000) is deterministic and parent-checkable exactly like decoded size, so the plan leaves a class of large text files with a misleading 'retry' that blocks close. That contradicts its own Product Intent and the Objective. The chair executed this on HEAD with a 1.26 MB, 210,000-line file.
strongest_alternative: Generalise 22qoz Requirement 1 into a parent-side pre-send check of every deterministic engine input cap (decoded bytes against MAX_CONTENT_BYTES and newline count against MAX_LINES), each with a distinct reason and the same remedy projection. This would be better: it closes the line-cap gap at the same small cost and with no ledger schema change, and it keeps the 22q2w policy. The red-team's surrogateescape alternative (scan such files fully) stays rejected for the line-hash churn the Decision Log records.

22qr5 N4: the worker computes the digest itself and refuses a mismatch with a new error code; the configured set lives on the process object.

falsification_check.working_verdict: Not ready: the 22qoz line-cap intent gap is a blocking readiness finding that needs an operator decision.
falsification_check.strongest_argument_against: The population is narrow (under 5 MiB with more than 200,000 lines, so average lines under about 26 bytes); the plan scoped engine caps out deliberately at the RT-1 repair; and the gap is pre-existing, not introduced by the wave, so it could be a follow-up.
falsification_check.why_it_does_not_change: The RT-1 scoping rationale (a shared detail) is factually inapplicable to the line cap, so the narrowing is a defect, not an accepted design choice. The plan's own AC priority treats 'no remedy' as required ('operators cannot recover'). The seed-209 derivation yields blocking do_now, and the chair may not reclassify to dodge it. The operator can still choose a follow-up via an explicit waiver or scope amendment.
